key_insight: Small-radius, high-electronegativity A-site dopants like Ca can simultaneously improve proton transport and chemical stability in BaCeO3-based perovskite electrolytes by weakening A–O bonding and contracting the lattice.
engineering_relevance: A-site doping offers a practical electrolyte design lever to boost proton uptake, reduce CO2/SO2 degradation, and potentially lower grain-boundary resistance in proton-conducting solid oxide fuel cells.
method: Mechanistic analysis of A-site electronegativity and ionic size effects
Assessment of proton transport, vacancy formation, and gas adsorption trends
evidence_signal: The abstract reports computational evidence that Ca doping strengthens proton uptake, suppresses impurity-phase formation, lowers CO2/SO2 adsorption, and may improve diffusion and grain-boundary behavior.
watch_item: Benefits may depend on whether proton transfer is the rate-limiting step, and Ca surface segregation or composition control could affect real-device reproducibility.
paper_title: Role of small-radius and high-electronegativity A-Site dopants in enhancing proton transport and stability of perovskite electrolytes
